headline: Five majors above their 200-day lines, whales quietly feeding exchanges, and the crowd feeling greedy anyway
paragraphs: Start with regime, because it's the cleanest read on this tape in a while. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB all sit above their 200-day lines, while DOGE and ADA sit below. That's five against two, a market with a majority trend intact rather than the mixed picture you get when it's split down the middle. ETH even shows a golden cross, the 50-day crossing up through the 200-day, which is a lagging confirmation of a trend already underway, not a new signal. BTC is up 20.0% on the month and ETH up 29.1% on the month, so the underlying structure has been constructive even if the last 24 hours look flat: BTC down -0.1% on the day, ETH down -0.0% on the day. Zoom to the week and the picture changes color: BTC down -0.9%, ETH down -3.9%, XRP down -7.1%, DOGE down -10.5%, ADA down -15.7%. Only SOL bucks that, up 8.4% on the week despite being down on the day. So the month says uptrend, the week says a pullback is in progress, and the day says pause. All three are true at once, they're just different windows on the same tape.

Momentum is where the divergence gets interesting. BTC's RSI-14 sits at 68.7, ETH at 66.4, SOL at 67.4, all comfortably warm without being pinned at extreme overbought, and all three carry MACD above signal, meaning the momentum indicator still leans bullish even as weekly price has cooled. That's a market where trend and momentum broadly agree even while the last five days chopped sideways to down. BNB is the odd one: price sits above its 200-day, but MACD has flipped below signal, a classic momentum-lagging-trend divergence worth flagging even though the 24-hour and monthly numbers still look fine. DOGE and ADA, the two below their 200-day lines, also show the weakest RSI readings on the board (53.3 and 47.4), so trend and momentum are at least honest with each other on the downside names.

Positioning tells you who's exposed and to what. BTC funding on OKX runs at 8.7% annualized, ETH at 3.4%, both positive, meaning longs are paying shorts to stay in the trade: a normal, unspectacular cost for a market that's been grinding up. SOL funding is negative at -8.8% annualized, an inversion where shorts are paying longs, odd company for an asset that's actually the week's best performer (+8.4%), and worth noting since it suggests the derivatives crowd hasn't fully bought the bounce. Open interest is largest in BTC ($2.14B) and ETH ($1.53B) on this venue, and liquidations over the past day lean hard toward longs getting flushed: BTC longs lost $13.6M against $4.2M for shorts, ETH longs lost $21.1M against $3.4M shorts, SOL longs lost $8.9M against $1.6M shorts. Long/short account ratios are elevated everywhere, from 1.12 on BTC up to 4.1 on DOGE and 2.47 on XRP, meaning retail accounts are stacked long across the board. Crowded longs plus one-sided liquidations is the kind of setup that makes a flat tape feel more fragile than the price action alone suggests.

Flows are the tension of the day. BTC ETFs printed a $201.9M outflow on 28 Aug, but the five-session net for BTC ETFs is a $924.5M inflow, a genuine disagreement between the daily print and the short trend (same_direction_days of just 1 confirms the daily figure is an outlier against its own recent run). ETH ETFs are cleaner: $102.1M inflow on the same day, $815.7M net over five sessions, ten straight days in the same direction, so that one actually earns a word like sustained. Meanwhile whale wallets have been moving the other way from the ETF headline: net $219.6M flowed onto exchanges over the last 72 hours, with BTC alone accounting for $164.7M onto exchanges and ETH another $55.0M. The weekly trend backs this up rather than looking like noise: net onto-exchange flow has grown every week for four straight readings, from $274M (week ending Aug 10) to $292M (Aug 17) to $807M (Aug 24) to $942M (Aug 31). Coins moving toward exchanges is usually read as potential sell-side supply staging, and it's happening in the same window that ETF five-day money is flowing in. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, is up only 1.3% over 30 days to $309.6B, not the kind of surge that suggests fresh buying firepower is piling in behind the ETF bid.

Sentiment sits at 62, Greed, inside its own 30-day range of 25 to 74, so the crowd is warm but not at the edges. That's a milder read than the derivatives book would suggest on its own, given the long-heavy account ratios and the one-sided liquidations. The tape underneath, rising exchange inflows for four straight weeks, a soft stablecoin float, and a BTC ETF daily print that broke from its own five-day trend, reads more cautious than the Greed label implies. What to watch from here: whether the onto-exchange whale flow keeps climbing on the next weekly read (a fifth straight increase would extend a real trend, not just noise), whether BTC ETF flows confirm the five-day inflow direction on the next daily print or revert again, and whether SOL's negative funding flips positive as its price sits above the 200-day, since that would mean derivatives traders are finally leaning into the move rather than fading it.
